title: Polynomial-time serialization of a wired group
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $c$ be a binary code for its optional states, and fix a template kind $K$. Suppose that each of the four functions producing unary words of lengths $m(x),s(x),t(x),p(x)$ is polynomial-time computable. Then the function sending $x$ to the serialized fragment of the clause group wired with those four parameters is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet
A binary code for its optional states
The unary functions $x\mapsto 1^{m(x)},1^{s(x)},1^{t(x)},1^{p(x)}$ are polynomial-time computable
replaced: For a fixed machine, state code, and template kind, if the unary input count, source time, target time, and selected index are polynomial-time computable, then the serialized fragment of the wired clause group is polynomial-time computable; only the unary wiring varies with the input.
